proposed_facts.reason: Canonical BuryWait collision unconditionally delegates to Bury collision. Its three short-circuit release conditions are failed custom-box collision, changed supporting-floor identity and a non-NULL stage descriptor. Ground_801C5700 dispatches on_touch_line or returns NULL; it does not explicitly test terrain motion. The functionality document agrees.

Canonical collision and release code support the stated conditions and ordinary BuryJump path. Independently inspected HammerWait and HammerJump definitions confirm that the early exception tests a held Hammer and enters HammerJump. Neither the proposal nor the document claims that all moving terrain necessarily remains valid.

contradictions.reason: Accept supersession of both static-floor claims. The actual guards concern support, floor identity and a nullable dynamics descriptor, not a categorical prohibition on moving terrain.

Accept rejection of both environmental-cooldown implements-buried-status links. Initialization and countdown operate on environmental timers whose consumers gate device/contact interactions; buried restraint separately initializes and reduces grab_timer and maintains motion-specific storage.

Accept unresolved dispositions for all three section claims. The conditional ordering helper shows source intent and literal references only. Without compiled evidence, section contents, placement, ordering and immutability remain deferred rather than established.

Accept the remaining cross-transition and effect-lifetime deferrals. Bury_Anim continues accessing move storage after release; effect updates also access buried-state storage. KeepGfx on BuryWait and its absence on ordinary BuryJump do not alone prove teardown safety for every exit, including HammerJump.
